definitions.explanation: The nutritive substances contained in food, soil, or other materials. More technical than {栄養|えいよう} alone — it refers to the constituent nutrient components rather than nutrition as a whole concept.

examples.japanese: この{野菜|やさい}は{栄養分|えいようぶん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This vegetable is high in nutrients.

examples.japanese: {土|つち}の{中|なか}の{栄養分|えいようぶん}が{植物|しょくぶつ}の{成長|せいちょう}を{支|ささ}える。
examples.english: The nutrients in the soil support plant growth.

examples.japanese: {加工食品|かこうしょくひん}は{調理|ちょうり}の{過程|かてい}で{栄養分|えいようぶん}が{失|うしな}われやすい。
examples.english: Processed foods tend to lose nutrients during the cooking process.

notes:
Compound of {栄養|えいよう} (nutrition) + {分|ぶん} (portion, component). Refers to specific nutritive components such as vitamins, minerals, proteins, and fats. Common in cooking, agriculture, and biology.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {栄養分|えいようぶん}が{多|おお}い: high in nutrients
- {栄養分|えいようぶん}を{摂|と}る: to take in nutrients
- {栄養分|えいようぶん}を{吸収|きゅうしゅう}する: to absorb nutrients
- {栄養分|えいようぶん}が{豊富|ほうふ}: rich in nutrients

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {栄養|えいよう}: nutrition — the broader concept; can also mean 'nutrients' in casual usage
- {栄養素|えいようそ}: nutrient (technical) — specific named nutrients in scientific contexts
- {養分|ようぶん}: nutrients — common in botany and agriculture; near-synonym
